mainTopic: When a rumor (קול) affects a woman's status: which rumors are ignored, what makes a rumor of קידושין count, when an אמתלא can cancel it, and whether courts cancel rumors.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a case: a rumor of קידושין that comes together with a rumor of divorce does not bind her, because the rumor 'carries its own receipt.' רבא rules that a rumor that a woman was a זונה is ignored, since people probably saw only פריצות. This matches רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who proves from the word 'דבר' that only a clear matter proven by witnesses counts. A ברייתא then lists rumors about status and property that we ignore. עולא, לוי, רבי יוחנן and רב each define the kind of rumor of קידושין that does count. It needs visible signs such as lit candles and made-up beds, or a trail of named sources who went overseas. רבי יוחנן adds that an אמתלא can cancel only a rumor that was not stated firmly. אביי and רב יוסף ask whether a court can cancel a rumor, and conclude that סורא does and נהרדעא does not. Real cases follow: רב חמא refuses a late explanation, and אביי cancels a rumor of betrothal with a mat of dates. A third case begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The woman counts as divorced
steps.stepSummary: The previous case ends with a ruling: she is considered divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling from the case right before this. Here a rumor that she was married came along with a rumor that she was divorced, and the ruling is that she counts as divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a rumor of קידושין is enough to treat a woman as married. Here the rumor of divorce came along with it, so the marriage rumor does not bind her. This short line sets up the question 'why?' that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: behold, this one is (introduces a ruling)

phrases.english: She is divorced.
phrases.notes: This finishes a case that started just before this text: a rumor of marriage that came together with a rumor of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a case begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the marriage rumor comes with a divorce rumor, she is treated as divorced.

steps.title: Why: the rumor comes with its own receipt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason and answers that the rumor carries its own cancellation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is a rumor that comes with its own receipt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why she counts as divorced. It answers that the rumor of marriage arrived together with the rumor that cancels it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שובר is a receipt that cancels a debt. In the same way, the divorce rumor 'cancels' the marriage rumor, so the marriage rumor never takes hold. A rumor only has power when nothing cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: a receipt that cancels a debt or claim

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is a rumor with its receipt along with it.
phrases.notes: The 'receipt' is the divorce rumor. It wipes out the marriage rumor the way a receipt wipes out a debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a rumor of marriage does not bind her here.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rumor came with its own cancellation (קול ושוברו עמו).

steps.title: רבא: a rumor that she was promiscuous is ignored
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a city-wide rumor that a woman was a זונה is not a concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if word went out in the city that she was a זונה, we are not concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule. A rumor in town that a woman was promiscuous does not change her status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rumor of קידושין is taken seriously, but רבא says a rumor of זנות is not. So she is not disqualified (for example, from marrying a כהן) because of talk alone.

keyTerms.meaning: a reputation, a name going around

phrases.english: Rava said:
If word went out in the city that she was promiscuous,
we are not concerned about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule about a different kind of rumor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rumor of זנות does not affect the woman's status.

steps.title: Why: they probably just saw loose behavior
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that people likely saw only immodest behavior, not an actual sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? People just saw her acting loosely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's rule. Whatever people saw was probably only immodest conduct, and that is not the sin itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rumor of קידושין is usually about a real event. A rumor of זנות often grows out of seeing immodest behavior and then exaggerating it. So the rumor proves only פריצות, and פריצות does not disqualify her.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is mere loose behavior that they saw in her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a rumor of זנות is ignored.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People likely saw only פריצות, not an actual sin.

steps.title: A dispute among תנאים: when must she leave her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links רבא's rule to a dispute among תנאים. רבי מאיר says immodest public acts force her to leave. רבי עקיבא says only when gossip spreads widely.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute among תנאים. If she ate in the market, strutted with her neck stretched out in the market, or nursed in the market: in all these cases רבי מאיר says she must leave her husband. רבי עקיבא says: only once the women spinning by moonlight talk about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבא's rule matches one side of an argument among the תנאים. It now quotes that argument, which continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats immodest public behavior as enough reason for her to leave her husband. רבי עקיבא needs more: real gossip about her actual sin, so widespread that even the women spinning at night talk about it. This sets the stage for רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who demands even more.

keyTerms.meaning: this matches a dispute of the תנאים
she walked haughtily with her neck stretched out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of evidence. רבי מאיר is talking about behavior people actually saw. רבי עקיבא is talking about gossip about her sin. These are not the same thing.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of Tannaim:
If she ate in the marketplace, strutted with outstretched neck in the marketplace,
or nursed in the marketplace,
in all of them Rabbi Meir says: she must leave.
phrases.notes: 'Leave' means her husband must divorce her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
only once they talk about her,
the women spinning by moonlight.
phrases.notes: The women who sit spinning thread at night and chat. It's a picture of gossip that has spread everywhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבא's rule matches one side of an earlier dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a rumor of זנות is ignored.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the dispute of רבי מאיר, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: no marriage would survive
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי objects that רבי עקיבא's standard would force every wife out of her marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said to him: if so, you have not left a single daughter of אברהם אבינו living with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי attacks רבי עקיבא's view. If gossip were enough, no marriage would be safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gossip about women is very common. If gossip alone forced a divorce, almost every wife would have to leave her husband. That result is absurd, so gossip cannot be the standard.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, לֹא הִנַּחְתָּ בַּת לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
phrases.english: If so, you have not left a daughter of Abraham our forefather
who remains living with her husband,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's position from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that widespread gossip forces her to leave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gossip is so common that his rule would end almost every marriage, which cannot be right.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'דבר': only a clear matter counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי proves from a גזירה שווה that the 'matter' in divorce must be clearly established by witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה says: 'Because he found in her an unseemly matter (דבר),' and elsewhere it says: 'By the word of two witnesses or three witnesses a matter (דבר) shall be established.' Just as there it means a clear matter, so too here it means a clear matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי backs up his objection with a proof from the פסוקים. He compares two places where the word 'דבר' appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about witnesses, 'דבר' means something proven by עדים. Through a גזירה שווה, the 'דבר' in the divorce פסוק must also be something clearly proven, not a rumor. This supports רבא: a rumor of זנות carries no weight.

keyTerms.meaning: learning one פסוק from another through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: Rumors have limits. A rumor cancelled by its own 'receipt' does not bind her. A rumor of זנות is treated as mere פריצות. According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, whose view matches רבא, only a clear matter proven by witnesses counts as ערות דבר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the standard that serious claims against a woman's status need real proof, not public talk.

phrases.english: And the Torah said:
"Because he found in her an unseemly matter,"
and over there it says:
"By the word of two witnesses

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יָקוּם דָּבָר״;
phrases.english: or by the word of three witnesses shall a matter be established";
just as there it is a clear matter,
so too here it is a clear matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן בן נורי's objection.
steps.raayaObject: That ערות דבר requires a clear, proven matter and not a rumor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שווה on the word 'דבר' from דברים 24:1 and דברים 19:15.

steps.title: A list of rumors we ignore
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists rumors about a woman's status, and rumors that a man gave away his property. In every case, אין חוששין: the rumor has no legal effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If people say a woman is a בעולה, we ignore it. If they say she is married, we ignore it. If they say she is betrothed, we ignore it. If they say she is betrothed but name no man, we ignore it. If they say she was betrothed in another city, we ignore it. If they say she is a ממזרת, we ignore it. If they say she is a שפחה, we ignore it. If they say a man made his property הקדש, or made it הפקר, we ignore these rumors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a list of rumors that the law does not take seriously. Each one ends with the same words: אין חוששין, we are not concerned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the theme from רבא's rule that a rumor alone does not change anyone's status. The list covers personal status (בעולה, married, betrothed, ממזרת, שפחה) and property (הקדש, הפקר). In none of these cases does gossip by itself change what we assume.

keyTerms.meaning: We are not concerned. The rumor has no legal effect.
A woman who is not a virgin
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A girl born from a forbidden relationship
He gave his property to the בית המקדש
He gave up ownership, so the property belongs to no one

steps.confusionAlert: This list says a plain rumor of betrothal (ארוסה) is ignored. The משנה, however, does treat a rumor of קידושין seriously. עולא's next statement explains the difference: the rumor that counts is not ordinary talk.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"A non-virgin" – we are not concerned about it.
"A married woman" – we are not concerned about it.
"A betrothed woman" – we are not concerned about it.
"Not to so-and-so" – we are not concerned about it.
phrases.notes: He means the rumor says she is betrothed but doesn't say to whom.

phrases.english: "In another city" – we are not concerned about it.
"A mamzeret" – we are not concerned about it.
"A maidservant" – we are not concerned about it.
"So-and-so consecrated his property";
"So-and-so renounced ownership of his property" – we are not concerned about these.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תנאים dispute about rumors of a wife's behavior, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with a wider list of rumors that are ignored.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rumors about a woman's personal status, or about a man giving away his property, have no legal effect.

steps.title: What kind of rumor of betrothal counts
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the rumor of קידושין in the משנה is not vague talk. It means visible signs that a betrothal is happening: lit candles, made-up beds, and people coming and going and saying she is getting betrothed today.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The rumor in the משנה does not mean people only heard an echo of talk. It means there are candles burning and beds made up, and people are going in and out saying, "So-and-so is getting betrothed today."
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defines the kind of rumor the משנה treats seriously. It is not loose gossip but a public scene that clearly shows a betrothal is taking place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא just said a plain rumor of betrothal is ignored. עולא shows that the rumor which counts is a different case: it comes with real signs, like a celebration in the house and people openly talking about it. Weak gossip does nothing, but clear, visible evidence does.

keyTerms.meaning: An echo of a rumor; vague talk with nothing behind it
Lit candles, a sign of a celebration
Beds made up and arranged, as was done for a bride

steps.whatToRemember: Plain gossip about someone's status is ignored. Only a rumor backed by clear, visible signs, like the scene עולא describes, is taken seriously.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard for when a rumor can affect a woman's status. Without such signs, people's talk cannot force anything.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Not where they heard an echo of a rumor;
rather, where there are candles burning
and beds made up,
and people coming in and going out
and saying: "So-and-so is getting betrothed today."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לֹא שֶׁשָּׁמְעוּ קוֹל הֲבָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא says rumors of betrothal are ignored, עולא defines the stronger kind of rumor that the משנה does treat seriously.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rumor of קידושין that counts must come with clear public signs of a betrothal, not mere hearsay.

steps.title: Challenging the words 'is getting betrothed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא's wording: if people only say she is getting betrothed today, maybe the betrothal never actually happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Is getting betrothed'?! Maybe in the end she was not betrothed at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the exact words עולא used in his description of the rumor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא described people saying 'so-and-so is getting betrothed today.' That only describes a plan for the future. Plans can fall through, so this kind of talk cannot make us treat her as truly married.

phrases.english: 'Is getting betrothed'?!
phrases.notes: This quotes the word עולא used in the previous step.

phrases.english: But perhaps she did not end up betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of עולא's description in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Talk about a future betrothal does not prove that a betrothal happened, so it cannot create a real rumor of קידושין.

steps.title: Fixing the wording to 'was betrothed today'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the wording should be read as 'so-and-so was betrothed today.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'So-and-so was betrothed today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording so that people are talking about a betrothal that already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the people are not guessing about the future. They are reporting that the betrothal took place today, so the rumor is strong enough to count.

phrases.english: Say instead:
'So-and-so was betrothed today.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People were only saying she would get betrothed, which is not enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: People are saying she already was betrothed today, which is a real rumor.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא gives the same picture
steps.stepSummary: לוי taught a ברייתא that a rumor of betrothal means real signs of celebration, not just a faint echo of talk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so לוי taught: it is not when people just hear an echo. It is when candles are lit, beds are made, and women spin by candlelight, rejoice for her, and say: 'So-and-so is getting betrothed today.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from לוי that supports עולא's description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like עולא, לוי says a vague echo is not enough. There must be visible signs of a celebration, plus people talking about her betrothal. He adds a new detail: women spinning by candlelight and rejoicing for her.

keyTerms.meaning: a faint echo of talk, a vague rumor

phrases.english: And so לוי taught:
Not when they only hear a faint echo;
rather, when there are candles burning
and beds made up,
and women spinning by the light of the candle
and rejoicing for her, and saying:
'So-and-so is getting betrothed today.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports עולא's description from Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's definition of a real rumor of קידושין

steps.title: The same wording problem in לוי's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the same problem with לוי's ברייתא: 'is getting betrothed' does not prove a betrothal happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Is getting betrothed'?! Maybe she was not betrothed in the end!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier challenge, now aimed at the words in לוי's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי's ברייתא uses the same future wording as עולא. So the same question comes back: talk of a betrothal that may still fall through should not count as a real rumor.

phrases.english: 'Is getting betrothed'?!
But perhaps she did not end up betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge from Step 10, now on לוי's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'פלונית מתקדשת היום' in לוי's ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A betrothal that is only about to happen might never happen.

steps.title: רב פפא fixes the wording of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא should be read as 'so-and-so was betrothed today.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Say instead: 'So-and-so was betrothed today.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the same fix to the ברייתא that the גמרא gave to עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is read as people reporting a betrothal that already happened. With the signs of celebration, this counts as a real rumor.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who gives this answer

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
Say instead: 'So-and-so was betrothed today.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אֵימָא: ״פְּלוֹנִית נִתְקַדְּשָׁה הַיּוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The women were only saying she would get betrothed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The women were saying she was already betrothed today.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: when it is a real rumor and when an explanation works
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also requires signs of celebration. If people spoke clearly about the betrothal, it is a real קול. If they did not, it is a case where an אמתלא can work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Not when people just heard a faint echo. Rather, when candles are lit, beds are made, and people go in and out. If they said something, that is a rumor. If they did not say something, that is a case for an explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement from רבי יוחנן describes a real rumor, and then divides it into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like עולא and לוי, רבי יוחנן needs visible signs of celebration. He then adds a split. If people stated it clearly, that is a full קול. If they did not, the case is weaker, and an אמתלא (an explanation) can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: a rumor that has legal weight
an explanation that weakens or cancels a rumor

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'did not say something' does not mean total silence. The next steps show that it means they did not say it clearly and firmly.

phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה said
that רבי יוחנן said:
Not when they only heard a faint echo;
rather, when there are candles burning
and beds made up,
and people going in and coming out.
If they said something, this is a rumor;
if they did not say something, this is an explanation case.
phrases.notes: He means this is the kind of case where an explanation can cancel the rumor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third description of a real rumor. This one adds the split between a full קול and an אמתלא case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Signs of celebration plus a clear statement make a real קול. Without a clear statement, an אמתלא can cancel it.

steps.title: If nothing was said, why is an explanation needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if they did not say anything, then there is nothing to explain away.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They did not say'?! But then they did not say anything at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's second case, 'they did not say something.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמתלא is only needed to cancel a rumor. If no one said anything, there is no rumor at all, so why talk about an explanation?

phrases.english: 'They did not say'?!
But then they did not say anything at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָמְרוּ?! וְהָא לֹא אָמְרוּ וְלֹא כְּלוּם!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last line of רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's phrase 'לא אמרו דבר זהו אמתלא'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Where nothing was said there is no rumor, so an explanation has nothing to cancel.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is arguing against רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן is ruling out רבה בר רב הונא's view that an explanation works even ten days later. An explanation only works when the people did not state it firmly.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to rule out רבה בר רב הונא, who said: an explanation that people give works even from now until ten days later. רבי יוחנן teaches us that only when they did not say it is there room for an explanation. But when they did say it, an explanation does not help.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing who רבי יוחנן is arguing with and what he is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא allowed an אמתלא to cancel a rumor even if it came up to ten days later. רבי יוחנן limits this. An explanation helps only where the rumor was not stated firmly. Once people clearly said she was betrothed, a later explanation cannot undo it.
steps.whatToRemember: A real rumor of קידושין needs visible signs of a betrothal, such as candles, made-up beds and people coming and going, and talk of a betrothal that already happened. According to רבי יוחנן, an אמתלא can cancel only a rumor that was not stated firmly. A firmly stated rumor cannot be undone by a later explanation, against רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a limit on how long, and in which cases, an explanation can undo a rumor that a woman is betrothed.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: This is to rule out רבה בר רב הונא, who said:
An explanation that people give
works even from now until ten days later.
So he teaches us:
only when they did not say it is it an explanation case;
phrases.notes: 'Did not say' means they did not say it clearly and firmly, not that they were silent.

phrases.english: but if they did say it, it is not an explanation case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16 by explaining what רבי יוחנן's words are meant to rule out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They did not say' looks pointless, since without talk there is no rumor at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן means that only a rumor that was not stated firmly can be canceled by an אמתלא. This rejects רבה בר רב הונא's ten-day allowance.

steps.title: רב defines a real rumor as one that can be traced
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the rumor in the משנה is not a vague murmur. It is one where people can say who heard it from whom, and the court investigates until it reaches a clear source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, who said it in the name of רב: The משנה does not mean that people just heard a vague murmur. It means that people can say: 'Where did so-and-so hear it? From so-and-so. And that person heard it from so-and-so.' The court keeps checking until it reaches something clear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains what kind of קול the משנה is talking about: a rumor with a trail of sources, not just a vague buzz.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rumor nobody can trace counts for nothing. רב requires a chain of names that the court can follow back. In this first version, the court follows the chain all the way to a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: A vague murmur or echo; talk with no clear source

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Not where they heard a vague murmur,
but rather where they can say:
Where did so-and-so hear it? From so-and-so;
and so-and-so heard it from so-and-so;
and they keep investigating
until they reach a clear matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement defining the rumor discussed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valid קול must be traceable person by person, and the court investigates until it reaches a clear source.

steps.title: If it ends in a clear fact, that is real testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the chain ends at a clear source, that is full testimony, not a rumor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A clear matter? That is full, proper testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's first version. If the court reaches eyewitnesses, we are no longer talking about a rumor at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is teaching a special rule about rumors. If רב's case ends with solid witnesses, the rumor adds nothing, because the witnesses would be enough by themselves. So this cannot be what רב meant.

phrases.english: A clear matter – that is proper testimony!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ending of רב's statement in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'until they reach a clear matter' in רב's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the trail ends at a clear source, that is real testimony, so the case is no longer about a rumor.

steps.title: The corrected version: the sources went overseas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different version of רב's statement, taught by רב שמואל בר יהודה. The chain of names exists, but the people in it went overseas, so the court cannot check further.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said in the name of רבי אבא, from רב הונא, from רב: Not where they heard a vague murmur. Rather, where they can say: 'Where did so-and-so hear it? From so-and-so. And that person from so-and-so.' And those people went overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first version and brings a corrected one. It keeps the chain of names but takes out the clear ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the rumor has real names behind it, so it is not a vague murmur. The court also cannot reach eyewitnesses, so it is not full testimony either. That puts it right in the middle, which is exactly the kind of rumor the משנה is about.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching
Overseas; far away and out of reach

steps.whatToRemember: A rumor that counts is in the middle. It has named sources behind it, so it is more than a murmur, but nobody can trace it to eyewitnesses, so it is less than testimony.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rather, when Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Not where they heard a vague murmur,
but rather where they can say:
Where did so-and-so hear it? From so-and-so;
and so-and-so heard it from so-and-so;
and they went away overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 19 by bringing a corrected version of רב's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's case ended with the court reaching a clear source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chain of names exists, but the people went overseas, so it stays a rumor and is not full testimony.

steps.title: אביי asks whether a rumor can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether a court can cancel or set aside a rumor.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Do we cancel a rumor, or do we not cancel it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. אביי asks whether a court can push aside a rumor that it could not confirm. The next steps will try to answer him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the discussion was about what makes a rumor count. This question asks the opposite: once a rumor is out, can the court treat it as nothing?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Do we cancel a rumor, or do we not cancel it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף מְבַטְּלִינַן קָלָא אוֹ לָא מְבַטְּלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whether a rumor can be cancelled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a court cancel or ignore a rumor?

steps.title: רב יוסף proves from רב חסדא that we cancel a rumor
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers from רב חסדא, who said a rumor only matters once it is heard from valid witnesses. This shows that rumors are treated lightly, so we can cancel them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since רב חסדא said 'only once they hear it from people who are כשרים,' learn from this that we cancel a rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by bringing a proof from what רב חסדא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא sets a high bar: a rumor only counts if it comes from people who are כשרים to testify. If rumors are held to such a strict standard before they count, that suggests they are weak and can be set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are valid to testify
Learn from this; conclude from it

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since Rav Chisda said:
'Only once they hear it from the mouths of valid people,'
learn from this: we cancel a rumor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁמְעוּ מִפִּי הַכְּשֵׁרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We cancel a rumor, as shown by רב חסדא's requirement that it come from valid people.

steps.title: אביי counters from רב ששת that we do not cancel a rumor
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the opposite. רב ששת said that even talk from women counts as a rumor, which shows rumors are taken seriously and cannot be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Just the opposite! Since רב ששת said that even from women it counts as a rumor, learn from this that we do not cancel a rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof with a teaching that points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women cannot testify in these matters, yet רב ששת still counts their talk as a rumor. If rumors are taken that seriously, they are not weak, so a court would not cancel them. Now there are two teachings pointing in opposite directions, and רב יוסף resolves this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Just the opposite; on the contrary

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא and רב ששת are not proving the same thing. רב יוסף reads רב חסדא's strict standard as a sign that rumors are weak, and אביי reads רב ששת's broad standard as a sign that rumors are strong.

phrases.english: He said to him: On the contrary!
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is אביי, answering רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Since Rav Sheshet said:
'Even from the mouths of women it counts as a rumor' –
learn from this: we do not cancel a rumor!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַדְּרַבָּה מִדְּאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof in step 22 by bringing an opposite indication.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's conclusion that we cancel a rumor
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ששת counts even women's talk as a rumor, which shows rumors are taken seriously and are not cancelled.

steps.title: It depends on the local custom
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge. The two views are local customs: סורא cancels rumors and נהרדעא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: These are the customs of different places. In סורא they cancel a rumor. In נהרדעא they do not cancel a rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge. He says רב חסדא and רב ששת are not really arguing; each one reflects the custom of a different city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 23, אביי used רב ששת to show that rumors are taken seriously, which seemed to contradict רב חסדא. רב יוסף says both are right, each in his own place. רב חסדא's lenient view matches סורא, where rumors are cancelled. רב ששת's strict view matches נהרדעא, where they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: They are different places, meaning each view follows a local custom
A major Babylonian city with a yeshiva
Another major Babylonian city with a yeshiva
They cancel or set aside a rumor

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a rumor of קידושין can be cancelled depends on local practice. סורא is lenient and נהרדעא is strict.

phrases.english: He said to him: These are different places;
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is answering אביי. Each opinion matches the custom of a different town.

phrases.english: in Sura they cancel a rumor,
in Nehardea they do not cancel a rumor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves אביי's challenge by assigning the two views to different local customs
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the views by place (local custom)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא and רב ששת disagree about whether a rumor can be cancelled
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are correct. סורא cancels rumors and נהרדעא does not

steps.title: A rumor about a yeshiva student, and רב חמא asks the father
steps.stepSummary: A rumor spread that a woman was betrothed to a yeshiva student. רב חמא calls her father and asks what really happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman about whom a rumor spread that she had been betrothed to a yeshiva student. רב חמא summoned her father and said to him: Tell me, how did the event happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a real-life case about a rumor of קידושין. רב חמא asks the father for the facts, which sets up the father's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of several case stories that show how courts handled rumors in practice. Before ruling, רב חמא wants to know the details of the betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain woman about whom a rumor went out

phrases.english: A certain woman about whom a rumor went out
that she was betrothed to a yeshiva student,
Rav Chama summoned her father,
he said to him: Tell me —
how did the event happen?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דִּנְפַק עֲלַהּ קָלָא דְּאִיקַּדַּשָׁה לְבַר בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general rule to a real case about a rumor
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual facts of how the betrothal took place

steps.title: The father says the betrothal was conditional
steps.stepSummary: The father explains that the student betrothed her on condition that he not go to בי חוזאי, and then he went, so the betrothal should be void.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father said to him: He betrothed her on a condition, with the understanding that he would not go to בי חוזאי, and he went.
steps.whatsHappening: The father answers רב חמא. He claims the קידושין fell apart because the condition was broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this is true, the betrothal was never valid, because the student broke his own condition. The father is offering an explanation that would make the rumor harmless.

phrases.english: He said to him: He betrothed on a condition,

phrases.aramaic: אַדַּעְתָּא דְּלָא אָזֵיל לְבֵי חוֹזַאי, וַאֲזַל.
phrases.english: with the understanding that he would not go to Bei Chozai, and he went.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חמא's question about the facts
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The betrothal depended on a condition that was later broken, so it is void

steps.title: A later explanation cannot undo the rumor
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא rules that because no explanation was known when the rumor spread, the father cannot add one now. The rumor stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא said to him: Since at the time the rumor spread there was no explanation, it is not in your power to establish an explanation now.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא rejects the father's explanation and rules strictly. The rumor stays in force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is what people heard when the rumor first spread. At that time, nobody mentioned any condition. An excuse brought in afterward cannot weaken a rumor that already took hold.

keyTerms.meaning: An explanation or excuse that weakens a rumor
It is not in your power

steps.confusionAlert: רב חמא does not say the father is lying. He says only that an explanation which was not part of the rumor from the beginning cannot cancel it later.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֵּיוָן דִּבְעִידָּנָא דַּהֲוַאי קָלָא –
phrases.english: He said to him: Since at the time that the rumor was —
there was no explanation,
it is not in your power to establish an explanation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the father's explanation and rejects it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An explanation that was not known when the rumor began cannot later cancel the rumor

steps.title: A betrothal with a mat of dates is brought to אביי
steps.stepSummary: A rumor spread that a woman was betrothed with a mat of dates at the spring of בי שיפי. רב אידי בר אבין asks אביי what the law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman about whom a rumor spread that she had been betrothed with a mat of dates at the spring of בי שיפי. רב אידי בר אבין sent the case to אביי: In a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case. רב אידי בר אבין asks אביי whether this rumor can be cancelled, which sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What stands out here is the object used for the betrothal: a mat of dates. That detail will matter, because people may doubt whether it was even worth enough to make the קידושין valid.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.english: A certain woman about whom a rumor went out,
that she was betrothed with a mat of dates,
at the spring of Bei Shifei.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחַהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin sent it before Abaye:
In a case like this, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דִּנְפַק עֲלַהּ קָלָא דְּאִיקַּדַּשָׁה בַּאֲצִיפָּא דְּתוּחְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second real case about a rumor
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a rumor of betrothal with a mat of dates can be cancelled

steps.title: Even the strict view cancels this rumor
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even the view that does not cancel rumors would cancel this one, because people will assume the Rabbis found the mat was worth less than a שוה פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Even according to the one who says we do not cancel a rumor, in this case we cancel the rumor. For people will say: The רבנן looked into her betrothal, and it was not worth a שוה פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that this rumor can be cancelled, even under the strict view of נהרדעא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict view worries that cancelling a rumor will make people gossip about the woman if she marries someone else. Here there is a simple explanation everyone will accept: a mat of dates may be worth less than a שוה פרוטה, so the קידושין never took effect. Since nobody will think badly of her, the rumor can be set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest value needed for קידושין
They looked into it, they checked

steps.whatToRemember: Even a strict court cancels a rumor when there is an obvious explanation people will accept, such as an object probably worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the strict view is about how the public will react. When a cancellation will not lead to gossip, even the strict view allows it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Even according to the one who says
we do not cancel a rumor,
in this case we cancel the rumor;
for people will say:
the Rabbis looked into her betrothal,
and it was not worth a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מְבַטְּלִינַן קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אידי בר אבין's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rumor is cancelled even under the strict view, because people will assume the dates were worth less than a פרוטה

steps.title: A third rumor case begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new case: a rumor spread that a certain woman was betrothed. The case continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman about whom a rumor spread that she had been betrothed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a third case story about a rumor of קידושין. The details come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words appear here. They follow the same pattern as the earlier cases, so expect another ruling on whether this rumor can be cancelled.

phrases.english: A certain woman about whom a rumor went out,
that she was betrothed
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where we hear how she was betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins another case in the same series of rumor stories
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. The case is still being introduced
